title: From Tears to Songs of Joy
overview: A song that remembers a time the LORD turned his people's fortunes around and asks him to do it again for troubles that remain.

parts.label: Like people dreaming (vv. 1-2a)
parts.note: The singers remember the LORD restoring Zion, meaning Jerusalem and its people, most likely when exiles came home from Babylon after 538 BC, though the psalm never names the event. The change felt so sudden and good that it seemed unreal, and they burst into laughter and song.

parts.label: Even outsiders noticed (vv. 2b-3)
parts.note: The surrounding nations, who had watched Israel's ruin, now said the LORD had done great things for these people. The singers repeat those words but make them their own: great things done for us.

parts.label: A prayer for more (v. 4)
parts.note: The mood turns to asking, because the restoration was not complete and the returned community likely still struggled. The Negev is the dry south, whose streambeds sit empty until rains suddenly flood them, so this is a plea for a sudden, life-giving change.

parts.label: Tears at planting, joy at harvest (vv. 5-6)
parts.note: Sowing was hard and risky, and in lean years seed put in the ground was food the family could not eat, so a farmer might plant in tears. The picture holds out hope that grief and labor now will give way to joy, like coming home with arms full of cut grain.

think: When something good has happened after a hard stretch, has it made the troubles that remained easier to carry, or harder?
